name: Handwritten Maths
description: Maths written by hand on lined paper, the way a teacher would see it: a student's worked equation and a long multiplication where the model must find the first wrong line and give the correct answer, a shopping list full of crossed-out corrections, a European hand whose 1s look like 7s (a correct example line shows the style), a recurrence written with subscripts, a word problem in crowded, messy capitals, plus stacked fractions and a power with a square root. The handwriting is a jittered single-stroke pen generated by code, so no image exists anywhere else.
hook: Mark the homework: find the mistake, read the mess, get the number.
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
The image shows a student's handwritten solution of an equation, with the lines numbered (1) to (5) in the margin. Line (1) is the equation to solve and is copied correctly. Exactly one later line contains the student's first mistake; every line after it follows on from that mistake. Which line contains the first mistake, and what is the correct value of x for the equation in line (1)?

End your reply with a JSON object in exactly this form: {"line": 3, "x": 12}
cases.notes: [hard] Lines: 4(x - 6) = 2x + 2 | 4x - 6 = 2x + 2 | 4x - 2x = 2 + 6 | 2x = 8 | x = 4. Correct working: 4x - 24 = 2x + 2 → 2x = 26 → x = 13. First wrong line: (2). Generated by verification/vision/handwriting.mts (seed 13201, hand 13301).

cases.prompt:
The image shows a student's handwritten long multiplication, with the lines numbered (1) to (5) in the margin: line (1) times line (2), the two partial products in lines (3) and (4), and their sum in line (5). Lines (1) and (2) are copied correctly. Exactly one of lines (3), (4) and (5) is wrong (a later line may add up a wrong line correctly). Which line is wrong, and what is the correct product of line (1) and line (2)?

End your reply with a JSON object in exactly this form: {"line": 4, "product": 12345}
cases.notes: [hard] Written: 859 | 47 | 6013 | 34460 | 40473. Correct: 859 × 7 = 6013, 859 × 40 = 34360, product 40373. Wrong line: (4). Generated by verification/vision/handwriting.mts (seed 13202, hand 13302).

cases.prompt:
The image shows a handwritten shopping list with corrections. Where a price is crossed out, the price written next to it replaces it; a line that is crossed out completely has been removed from the list. What is the total of the list as it now stands?

Give the final answer as a single number with two decimals (for example 12.30), no currency sign. Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [hard] Items: EGGS 7.68 (removed), RICE 8.07→7.47, BREAD 7.42, COFFEE 3.92, CHEESE 6.27, APPLES 4.84→5.34. Total 30.42. Generated by verification/vision/handwriting.mts (seed 13203, hand 13303).

cases.prompt:
The image shows two lines of handwritten arithmetic by the same person. The first line is a correct worked example; it shows how this person writes their digits. Work out the value of the expression on the second line (multiplication before addition and subtraction).

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [hard] European-style hand: 1 is drawn as a long upstroke with no foot (it can look like an uncrossed 7) and 7 carries a crossbar. Calibration line 17 + 71 = 88 (correct). Written: (711 − 77) × 7 + 71 = 634 × 7 + 71 = 4509. Generated by verification/vision/handwriting.mts (seed 13204, hand 13304).

cases.prompt:
The image shows a handwritten sequence definition using subscripts (small numbers and letters written below the line), and a question on the last line. What is the answer to the question?

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [hard] Written: a_1 = 3; a_(n+1) = 2·a_n − 1; a_6 = ?. Sequence: 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, 65. Generated by verification/vision/handwriting.mts (seed 13205, hand 13305).

cases.prompt:
The image shows a word problem handwritten quickly in crowded capital letters. Solve it.

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
cases.notes: [hard] Written: "TOM HAS 60 STAMPS. HE BUYS 4 PACKS OF 12 AND GIVES HALF OF ALL HIS STAMPS TO HIS SISTER. THEN HE BUYS 33 MORE. HOW MANY DOES HE HAVE NOW?" → 60 + 4 × 12 = 108; half = 54; + 33 = 87. Messy, tightly spaced hand. Generated by verification/vision/handwriting.mts (seed 13206, hand 13306).

cases.prompt:
The image shows a handwritten expression with two stacked fractions inside brackets, multiplied by a whole number. What is its value?

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.

The image shows a handwritten expression with a power (a small raised exponent), a square root and a division sign. Work it out using the usual order of operations.

Give the final answer as a single integer (digits only, no words or units). Give exactly one answer. If you give more than one answer, it will be marked wrong.
